headline: Approved an accessory dwelling unit at 240 Lothrop Street; paving at 12 Greenwood Avenue continued to November 17.
summary: Issued a Negative 3 Determination for a garage replacement at 45 Cole Street, and approved tree removals at 19 Yankee Way and 28 Cliff Street. Denied a request to add a seawall maintenance condition at 385 & 407 Hale Street. Continued the 24 Whitehill Circle and 58 Middlebury Lane items to November 17, 2026.
decisions: Continued the 24 Whitehill Circle patio and retaining wall request to November 17, 2026, 4-0.
Tabled the 58 Middlebury Lane deck and workshop ceiling item because no representative was present.
Issued a Negative 3 Determination of Applicability with conditions for 45 Cole Street, 4-0.
Issued a Complete Certificate of Compliance for 1 Brookwood Road, 4-0.
Approved the minor modification at 0 Longham Road, 4-0.
Approved the minor modification at 343 Dodge Street with conditions, 4-0.
Approved a one-year extension to December 15, 2027, under the local ordinance and a three-year extension to December 15, 2029, under the Wetlands Protection Act for 385 & 407 Hale Street, 4-0.
Approved the tree removal request at 19 Yankee Way with conditions, 4-0.
Tabled the 28 Cliff Street tree removal request because the applicant had technical issues.
Approved the tree removal request at 28 Cliff Street with conditions, 4-0.
Continued the 58 Middlebury Lane item to November 17, 2026, 4-0.
Continued the 12 Greenwood Avenue hearing on the driveway paving request to November 17, 2026, 4-0.
Denied the request to amend the order for 385 & 407 Hale Street to add a seawall maintenance condition, 4-0.
Amended the enforcement order for 25 Linden Avenue to require removal of cut waste in the resource area and attendance at the November 17, 2026 meeting, 4-0.
Ratified the enforcement order issued to 2 Robin Road, 4-0.
Amended the 2 Robin Road enforcement order to require a Request for Determination of Applicability by November 2, 2026, 4-0.
Approved a $215 reimbursement to Greg Power for MACC fundamentals training, 4-0.
Approved a $100 donation for a Greenbelt membership, 4-0.
Issued an Order of Conditions for 240 Lothrop Street, 4-0.
Approved the October 6, 2026 meeting minutes as amended, 4-0.

CITY OF BEVERLY  1

LOCATION:  Virtual via Google Meet 6 
MEMBERS PRESENT:  Chair Christine Bertoni, Robert Buchsbaum, William 7 
Squibb, Joanne Miller 8 
MEMBERS ABSENT:  Greg Power 9 
STAFF PRESENT:  Conservation Agent David Spidaliere, Field Inspector Scott 10 
White 11 
 12 
 13 
1.  Call to Order 14 
Chair Bertoni calls the meeting to order at 6:30 p.m. and conducts a roll call. A quorum of seated 15 
members is present. Bertoni reads the public notice regarding holding meetings remotely due to 16 
COVID-19 provisions. 17 
 18 
2.  Requests for Determination of Applicability 19 
 a. New: 24 Whitehill Circle – expand an existing patio and install a retaining  20 
  wall – Michael Vigorito 21 
 22 
Spidaliere reads the public legal notice. 23 
 24 
Michael Vigorito, applicant, notes that he is a member of the Beverly Planning Board and 25 
Community Preservation Committee. This is a Request for Determination for a patio extension in 26 
the rear yard. The lot was permitted in 2009 under DEP File #5-1016. The Certificate of 27 
Compliance was recorded in 2016. The proposed work is a bluestone terrace extension with a 3’-28 
4’ stone face retaining wall. This will be no closer than 50’ to the wetland, with erosion controls 29 
downgradient to the extent required. The existing bluestone patio has a grass area next to it 30 
which drops to a cliff with some boulders. This is fairly dangerous for children and visitors. The 31 
intention is to extend the existing patio outwards. There is an existing fence that currently closes 32 
in the area which is proposed to be replaced with a retaining wall.  33 
 34 
Bertoni notes that the proposal is for 600 s.f. of new terrace on existing lawn. The proposal is to 35 
use stone dust under the patio extension, but this will become an impervious surface. She asks 36 
about grading for the retaining wall. Vigorito explains that the existing lawn area is 37 
approximately 2”-3” lower than the existing blue stone patio. There may need to be some dirt 38 
brought in to level this area. In terms of the stone dust, he explains that he was told the stone dust 39 
and crushed gravel will be best to filter the area, instead of a concrete slab. Bertoni asks about a 40 
grading plan. Vigorito states that there is not an engineered plan, the hope is to build a patio 41 
directly over the existing lawn area. One possibility is to make the patio extension a bit smaller, 42 
so no fill would be required. 43 
 44
City of Beverly Conservation Commission  
October 27, 2026  
  Meeting Minutes  
 
Page 2 of 11 
 
In response to a question from Buchsbaum, Vigorito explains that the aluminum fence will be 45 
removed, but the chain-link fence will remain. 46 
 47 
Bertoni suggests a site visit. The No Build Zone is 50’ from the edge of wetland and this needs to 48 
be shown on the plan. She asks if the retaining wall will be level with the ground. Vigorito states 49 
that it will be.  50 
 51 
Buchsbaum asks when the wetlands were last delineated. Vigorito states that he believes this was 52 
done in 2009 or 2011.  53 
 54 
Bertoni states that, due to the proposed earth movement and the way it is proposed, a site visit 55 
would be a good idea, and she has some concerns about this work being permitted via an RDA. 56 
 57 
The Commission agrees to a site visit on October 31st at 8am. 58 
 59 
Buchsbaum:  Motion to continue this RDA to November 17, 2026. Miller seconds. Bertoni  60 
  takes a roll call vote. Motion carries (4-0). 61 
 62 
 b. New: 58 Middlebury Lane – expand an existing deck and install a ceiling  63 
  under  the deck for a workshop area – Daniel Guley 64 
 65 
Spidaliere reads the public legal notice. 66 
 67 
The Commission agrees to table this item to later in the meeting, as a representative was not 68 
present. 69 
 70 
 c. New: 45 Cole Street – demolish an existing garage and construct an addition  71 
  in its place – Robert Freni 72 
 73 
Spidaliere reads the public legal notice. 74 
 75 
Robert Freni, representing the homeowner, explains that the property contains an existing 76 
garage. The 100’ wetland buffer barely hits the edge of the garage. The proposal is to demolish 77 
the existing single level garage and construct a new garage, mostly keeping the same footprint on 78 
the front and rear side of the building, but expanding to the west approximately 3’ and building a 79 
new primary bedroom on the second level. The applicant is also proposing a covered porch in the 80 
front of the structure. A certified plot plan was submitted overlaid with the buffer zone map. 81 
These are two areas that will be under construction. The front porch will be 80’ from the wetland 82 
edge.  83 
 84 
Bertoni asks if there is an existing foundation. Freni states that there is one, but it has been 85 
determined that this would not support two levels, so the existing foundation will also be 86 
demolished. This is 3’ below grade. A frost wall will be installed in its place at 4’ deep. 87 
 88
City of Beverly Conservation Commission  
October 27, 2026  
  Meeting Minutes  
 
Page 3 of 11 
 
Bertoni notes that there will be an increased amount of impervious surface on the site based on 89 
the proposed covered porch installation. Freni explains that the roof runoff will be about the 90 
same. There will be gutters in the front and back to bring the runoff down to the soil to percolate 91 
in a crushed stone area around the foundation. Silt fence will be installed during demolition. The 92 
garage tested positive for asbestos, and a certified professional will remove this prior to 93 
demolition. The covered porch will be on four sonotubes. 94 
 95 
Buchsbaum:  Motion to issue a Negative 3 Determination of Applicability with conditions as 96 
discussed. Miller seconds. Bertoni takes a roll call vote. Motion carries (4-0). 97 
 98

Removals/Emergency Certifications 100 
 a. Certificates of Compliance 101 
  i. New: 1 Brookwood Road, DEP File #5-1061 102 
 103 
Jordan Foulds, DeRosa Environmental, explains that at the last meeting an Enforcement Order 104 
was lifted for the mitigation plantings required under this permit. The applicant now requests a 105 
Complete Certificate of Compliance. 106 
 107 
Bertoni notes a number of perpetual conditions that will be included. 108 
 109 
Buchsbaum:  Motion to issue a Complete Certificate of Compliance for 1 Brookwood Road, 110 
DEP File #5-1061, including perpetual conditions #38-42 and perpetual special 111 
conditions #1.d., 1.e., 1.f., 2.a., 2.g., 2.h., 4.e., 4.f. & 4.g. Squibb seconds. Bertoni 112 
takes a roll call vote. Motion carries (4-0). 113 
 114 
 b. Minor Modifications to Orders of Conditions 115 
  i. New: 0 Longham Road, DEP File #5-1382 116 
 117 
Nathan Mousseau, Salem/Beverly Water Supply Board, explains that at the October 6th meeting, 118 
a hazardous tree removal application was submitted for four trees that would be a direct impact 119 
to the proposed construction and excavation at the property. During that meeting it was 120 
determined that the hazardous removal was approved based on certain conditions. One of those 121

 123 
Buchsbaum:  Motion to approve the Minor Modification at 0 Longham Road, DEP File #5-124 
1382. Squibb seconds. Bertoni takes a roll call vote. Motion carries (4-0). 125 
 126 
  ii. New: 343 Dodge Street, DEP File #5-1476 127 
 128 
Jordan Foulds, DeRosa Environmental, explains that the proposal is for eight trees to be removed 129 
by crane: seven ash and one hemlock. These trees are all dead and the ash trees have been 130 
affected by the emerald ash borer. The applicant is proposing replacement trees, including three 131 
red oak and five red maple. 132 
 133
City of Beverly Conservation Commission  
October 27, 2026  
  Meeting Minutes  
 
Page 4 of 11 
 
Bertoni notes that the tree debris will be removed from the site and that there will be no stump 134 
grinding. The replacement trees require 100% survival after two years. 135 
 136 
Buchsbaum:  Motion to approve the Minor Modification at 343 Dodge Street, DEP File #5-137 
1476 with the conditions as discussed. Squibb seconds. Bertoni takes a roll call 138 
vote. Motion carries (4-0). 139 
 140 
 c. Extensions to Orders of Conditions 141 
  i. New: 385 & 407 Hale Street, DEP File #5-1348 142 
 143 
Benjamin Foley, representing the applicant, explains that the request is to extend the open Order 144 
of Conditions for the project to allow for any unplanned maintenance over the next year. 145 
Extending this Order will allow for any loose stones to be picked up and replaced, concrete crack 146 
repairs, etc.  147 
 148 
Spidaliere explains that the original expiration date was December 15, 2024, but it was auto 149 
extended with Permit Extension Act to December 15, 2026. This request is for a one-year 150 
extension under the local ordinance to December 15, 2027, and a three-year extension under the 151 
Wetlands Protection Act to December 15, 2029. 152 
 153 
Foley explains that the original project was completed as proposed but the proposed extension 154 
allows for necessary repairs to be done. The seawall has a Chapter 91 license. Any repairs made 155 
would require notification to the Commission.  156 
 157 
Buchsbaum:  Motion to issue a one-year extension to December 15, 2027, under the local 158 
ordinance and a three-year extension to December 15, 2029, under the Wetlands 159 
Protection Act. Miller seconds. Bertoni takes a roll call vote. Motion carries (4-0). 160 
 161 
 d. Tree Removals 162 
  i. New: 28 Cliff Street 163 
 164 
The Commission tables this item due to the applicant experiencing technical issues. 165 
 166 
  ii. New: 19 Yankee Way 167 
 168 
Peter Vonzweck, owner, explains that the request is to remove three trees: two poplars and one 169 
Tree of Heaven. The trees are leaning and there is a potential hazard to hit a neighbor’s house. 170 
These trees are above a drainage system and if they fall there could be damage to an existing 171 
berm. The proposed removal will be from an existing paved area by crane. The bottoms will be 172 
saw cut and root systems left in place. The side of the berm should not have vegetation on it, so 173 
no replacement trees are proposed.  174 
 175 
Buchsbaum:  Motion to approve the tree removal request at 19 Yankee Way, with the 176 
conditions as discussed. Miller seconds. Bertoni takes a roll call vote. Motion 177 
carries (4-0). 178
City of Beverly Conservation Commission  
October 27, 2026  
  Meeting Minutes  
 
Page 5 of 11 
 
 179 
  i. New: 28 Cliff Street 180 
 181 
The Commission retakes this item. 182 
 183 
Maureen Driscoll, owner, states that the trees on site are invasive, tree of heaven trees. She is 184 
requesting to remove them. She would like to stabilize the bank with native plants. A more 185 
permanent way to stabilize the bank may be needed in the future. 186 
 187 
Bertoni notes that these trees seem to be growing on Coastal Bank. This work is proposed within 188 
Riverfront Area, but staff has indicated that the Commission has allowed for tree removal via a 189 
hazard tree removal permit in resource areas in the past. 190 
 191 
Buchsbaum notes that this stretches the definition of a hazard tree removal and the Commission 192 
may want to reconsider the definition to add removal of invasive trees in the future. 193 
 194 
Buchsbaum:  Motion to approve the tree removal request at 28 Cliff Street, with the conditions 195 
as discussed. Squibb seconds. Bertoni takes a roll call vote. Motion carries (4-0). 196 
 197 
b. New: 58 Middlebury Lane – expand an existing deck and install a ceiling   198 
 under  the deck for a workshop area – Daniel Guley 199 
 200 
The Commission retakes this item and notes that the applicant is still not present at the meeting, 201 
so they agree to continue this item to the next meeting. 202 
 203 
Squibb:  Motion to continue this item to November 17, 2026. Miller seconds. Bertoni takes 204 
a roll call vote. Motion carries (4-0). 205 
 206 
4.  Recess for Public Hearings  207 
 208 
Squibb:  Motion to recess for Public Hearings. Buchsbaum seconds. Bertoni takes a roll 209 
call vote. Motion carries (4-0). 210 
  211 
5.  Notices of Intent/Abbreviated Notices of Intent/Requests for Amended Orders of 212 
Conditions/Abbreviated Notices of Resource Area Delineations 213 
a. Cont.: 240 Lothrop Street, DEP File #5-1481 – construct an Accessory 214 
Dwelling Unit and deck – Sean & Nicole Hartley 215 
 216 
Mary Trudeau, representing the applicants, states that since the first meeting with the 217 
Commission, a site visit was held. The contractor was present and spoke about the helical piles 218 
that he plans on using instead of a foundation. The Commission was able to see the waterway 219 
and the area to be replanted with native shrubs. The proposed accessory dwelling unit (ADU) 220 
will be 20’x32’. The contractors have suggested a 2’x2’ stone filled trench around the perimeter 221 
of the new ADU to act as a holding area for stormwater runoff.  222 
 223
City of Beverly Conservation Commission  
October 27, 2026  
  Meeting Minutes  
 
Page 6 of 11 
 
Bertoni asks for public comment.  224 
 225 
Spidaliere reads two letters of support, one from Kenneth Weafer, owner of 242 East Lothrop 226 
Street, and the other from Josh Doxsee at 244 East Lothrop Street. Both letters express that the 227 
proposal reflects thoughtful planning and responsible property stewardship, and request that the 228 
Commission approve the proposal. 229 
 230 
There is no additional public comment. 231 
 232 
Buchsbaum:  Motion to close the hearing for 240 Lothrop Street, DEP File #5-1481. Squibb 233 
seconds. Bertoni takes a roll call vote. Motion carries (4-0). 234 
 235 
b. New: 12 Greenwood Avenue, DEP File #5-1447 – request to amend Order of 236 
Conditions –  14 Greenwood Beverly, LLC 237 
 238 
Spidaliere reads the public legal notice. 239 
 240 
Michael Paige, Griffin Engineering, explains that this is a request to amend an Order of 241 
Conditions issued by the Conservation Commission on July 2, 2025. This was for work 242 
associated with a new single family residence at 12 Greenwood Avenue, including installation of 243 
a force main and improvements to the common driveway. The force main is already installed and 244 
connected. The construction of the driveway for 12 Greenwood Avenue is complete and this also 245 
included common driveway improvements such as widening the common driveway to 14’ for 246 
accessibility purposes. The amended request is to pave the recently widened common driveway. 247 
Widening the driveway improved conditions but, based on the slope of the driveway, frequently 248 
needed gravel maintenance, and the fact that the driveway is essentially impervious due to the 249 
slope, paving is preferred. The Beverly Fire Department and the several of the property owners 250 
who utilize the common driveway are in support of updating the common driveway for safety 251 
and maintenance purposes. Paving the driveway will improve access for vehicles, including 252 
emergency vehicles; maintenance will be reduced; driveway erosion will be eliminated, reducing 253 
accumulation of silt and gravel in the drainage ditch and the wetlands, which improves water 254 
quality; and gravel will no longer be deposited in snowbanks along the driveway. An amendment 255 
is appropriate to the Order as it is associated with improvements of the common driveway which 256 
was associated with the single family construction at 12 Greenwood Avenue. The driveway will 257 
not be made any larger than the existing common driveway with its widening to 14’.  258 
 259 
Bertoni notes that the Commission has no obligation to hear amendments but tends to consider 260 
them. MassDEP had a number of comments for the initial project, one of which was to leave the 261 
driveway as a gravel road. This is adjacent to a wetland and a wetland replication needed to be 262 
installed based on encroachment. The road surface appears to not be adequate to apply asphalt 263 
and would need to be further compacted. Paige stated that a bit of a gravel will be installed 264 
below the pavement to create a crest, but no additional compacting is needed.  265 
 266
City of Beverly Conservation Commission  
October 27, 2026  
  Meeting Minutes  
 
Page 7 of 11 
 
Ben Carlson, applicant, explains that a road maintenance agreement is being proposed with the 267 
neighbors as part of this project. It has not yet been decided if the roadway will be paved or not. 268 
This is being offered in case the neighbors are in favor of reduced maintenance and better access. 269 
 270 
Bertoni states that winter treatment and potential additional runoff based on the proposed 271 
pavement could be concerns. Carlson states that the majority of the neighbors are ready to create 272 
a roadway maintenance agreement, but not all are in favor.  273 
 274 
Spidaliere notes that the applicant should reach out to the Assistant Planning Director to discuss 275 
the definitive subdivision plan and if any pavement details need to be added or modified. 276 
Secondly, the Engineering Department submitted the following comments: “We find the 277 
submission presented to be insufficient as it is missing critical information to review. We have 278 
the following comments. 1) provide stormwater management calculations for newly proposed 279 
impervious common driveway. 2) provide a condition assessment of the existing 4” cast iron 280 
culvert located near station 950 in terms of its structural integrity and suitability for continued 281 
use. 3) provide additional information regarding the existing culvert on Greenwood Ave. that 282 
receives flow from the drainage ditch, including size, capacity, material condition. 4) provide 283 
pavement detail for the post roadway improvements, including the proposed pavement structure 284 
and base materials. 5) Greenwood Avenue is an existing steep and narrow roadway with limited 285 
shoulder space. This office has previously expressed concerns regarding snow storage, snow 286 
removal operations, and potential roadway icing. The applicant should provide an operation and 287 
maintenance plan for the roadway. 6) during construction phase activities, excavation and 288 
earthwork shall be done in compliance with erosion control rules and regulations. Open areas of 289 
the surface and soil/material stockpiles should be protected from waterborne and windborne 290 
erosion and shall not have any negative impact on surrounding privately owned or municipally 291 
owned property. 7) the applicant is reminded that a stormwater O&M is due annually to the 292 
Engineering Department by December 31st of every calendar year. Commencement of work 293 
acknowledges that noncompliance with this requirement is subject to violations and applicable 294 
fees and fines. This reporting requirement is also valid for all construction related activities.” 295 
 296 
The Commission agrees to hold a site visit on November 8th at 11am. 297 
 298 
Buchsbaum asks about the potential use of pervious material and/or if the entire driveway needs 299 
to be paved. Paige notes that pervious pavement may not be possible based on the slope of the 300 
roadway.  301 
 302 
Bertoni asks for public comment.  303 
 304 
Charlie Dunn, 16 Greenwood Avenue, states that he is in favor of the proposal for maintenance 305 
reasons. He asks that the drainage ditches be improved as much as possible in order to handle 306 
any additional runoff. 307 
 308 
Spidaliere reads two letters of public comment. One from the owner of 14 Greenwood Avenue 309 
expressed support for approval of the proposed paving of the shared driveway. The second, from 310 
the owner of 4 Greenwood Avenue, Philip Thomason, explains that the road is an easement over 311
City of Beverly Conservation Commission  
October 27, 2026  
  Meeting Minutes  
 
Page 8 of 11 
 
his property. Contrary to the letter of amendment dated October 13, 2026, the property owners 312 
did not collectively request that the roadway be paved. The contractor has proposed this to them. 313 
He and his wife are fully against paving. There are drainage issues and paving over this road 314 
could lead to frost heaves, potholes, and erosion of the pavement which will be washed into the 315 
surrounding environment. Sand and salt runoff may run into the wetland resources. This roadway 316 
is heavily shaded with steep grades in some sections. The gravel road provides traction in winter 317 
conditions. A paved road will lead to black ice, requiring more extensive sanding and salting. 318 
The sand and salt will wash down into the wetland areas including the vernal pool. Paving was 319 
not a condition of a legal agreement with the abutters, which was included in the issuance of the 320 
original special permit.  321 
 322 
There is no additional public comment. 323 
 324 
Carlson notes that he has a legal right to make the road safe for pass and repass, as does any 325 
other owner that uses the right of way, without the permission of others. 326 
 327 
Buchsbaum:  Motion to continue the hearing for 12 Greenwood Avenue, DEP File #5-1447, to 328 
November 17, 2026. Miller seconds. Bertoni takes a roll call vote. Motion carries 329 
(4-0). 330

c. New: 385 & 407 Hale Street, DEP File #5-1348 – request to amend Order of 332 
Conditions – Endicott College c/o Rick Gagnon 333 
 334 
Spidaliere reads the public legal notice. He explains that the legal ad was run ahead of MassDEP 335 
comments. MassDEP determined that the additional work proposed cannot be permitted under an 336 
amended Order of Conditions. The applicant has updated this amendment request to include only 337 
an additional perpetual condition. 338 
 339 
Benjamin Foley, representing the applicant, explains that a modification was submitted for an 340 
amendment to the existing Order of Conditions. The request is for the Commission to consider a 341 
perpetual condition to allow for maintenance and minor repairs to the existing seawall. 342 
 343 
Bertoni states that this is not to work on additional revetment areas but to include a perpetual 344 
condition for maintenance on the seawall that was already built. Foley explains that the applicant 345 
will be filing a Notice of Intent to apply for a new Order of Conditions, separate from the work 346 
originally authorized in areas A, B, and C. Bertoni notes that this has a Chapter 91 license that 347 
allows for routine maintenance. Foley asks if this covers work under the Wetland Protection Act. 348 
Spidaliere explains that a DEP analyst confirmed that they do not prefer amending Orders of 349 
Conditions to add perpetual conditions, especially ones which would impact Coastal Bank or 350 
other resource areas. Chapter 91 covered repairs will still require the filing of a Notice of Intent 351 
if they will impact resource areas. If there are not impacts to resource areas, then this would be 352 
covered by Chapter 91 and require notification the Commission. Foley explains that maintenance 353 
repair work would take unauthorized stones outside of the authorized Order of Conditions area 354 
and bring them into the structure limit. Bertoni notes that she is not in favor of adding a perpetual 355 
condition as the details of the future maintenance are unclear.  356
City of Beverly Conservation Commission  
October 27, 2026  
  Meeting Minutes  
 
Page 9 of 11 
 
 357 
Foley states that it appears any minor repairs should at least be filed through an RDA 358 
application. Bertoni agrees. 359 
 360 
There is no public comment. 361 
 362 
Buchsbaum:  Motion to deny the amendment request for 385 & 407 Hale Street, DEP File #5-363 
1348. Miller seconds. Bertoni takes a roll call vote. Motion carries (4-0). 364 
 365

 367 
Squibb:  Motion to reconvene the meeting. Miller seconds. Bertoni takes a roll call vote. 368

7. Enforcement Matters/Potential Violations 371 
a. Enforcement Orders 372 
i. Cont.: 25 Linden Avenue – Leslie Salter 373 
 374 
Leslie Salter, homeowner, explains that she submitted an invoice showing that she paid for the 375 
yard waste to be removed. She believed everything was moved up to the yard, but this was not 376 
the case. She thinks this work will now be done this week. 377 
 378 
Buchsbaum:  Motion to amend the Enforcement Order for 25 Linden Avenue to require 379 
removal of the cut waste in the resource area and require attendance at the 380 
November 17, 2026, meeting. Miller seconds. Bertoni takes a roll call vote. 381 
Motion carries (4-0). 382 
 383 
ii. New: 2 Robin Road – Norman Papazian 384 
 385 
John Aponas, contractor representing the applicant, explains that the existing pool is being 386 
renovated, including the concrete apron. The profile will be shrunk to 4’. The water being 387 
pumped from the pool is clean and there is a high water table. The creek is about 40’ away from 388 
the deck edge of the pool. They did not realize that they needed to file with the Conservation 389 
Commission for this work. 390 
 391 
Bertoni states that pumping any type of water into the resource area is a violation of the 392 
Wetlands Protection Act. This must be filtered through something. Aponas states that this can be 393
